correctness.rationale: The 2022 primary source Defines 1-Minkowski weights by vector balancing on each 2-face (Definition4.1) and normalizes ∑edges ω(E)=f1(P) (Definition4.3). Triangle and product square face equations propagate a unique weight λ_i to every edge moving in simplex factor i. Exactly E_i=C(d_i+1,2)∏_{j≠i}(d_j+1)=Vd_i/2 edges are of class i, giving ∑ d_i λ_i=D. Orthogonal disjoint classes make y_i=√E_i λ_i a genuine isometry into a coordinate simplex with normal a_i=√d_i and ∥a∥²=D. The projection of e_i to its tangent plane has norm √((D−d_i)/D); therefore facet clearance δ_i=y_i√(D/(D−d_i)). Equalizing all facet clearances uniquely gives r=D^(3/2)√(V/2)/S and λ_i*=D/S √((D−d_i)/d_i); this is a globally maximal inball because any radius r imposes all k coordinate inequalities and their weighted sum bounds r. Pure-factor vertices have pairwise disjoint supports, yielding the squared-distance formula; all sides equal for k≥3 iff all d_i equal; any k=2 case is a segment. The d-cube specialization checked. Independent cases d=(1,1),(1,2,3),(2,3,4),(3,3,3) yield identical facet clearances and exact normalization. General theorem is symbolic, not inferred from these cases.
